data.content_ref: inline:015994869366 contradicts SRC_003's analogy claim that the explicit-procedure/implicit-capacity confound is symmetric between human panels and models. For a human panel, the implicit reasoning capacity is external to the frozen theory and can be independently probed; for a model, the mapping and the implicit capacity are the same substrate, so the confound is structural and cannot be decoupled by any evaluation strategy available to the panel. This asymmetry is refuted if the model's implicit capacity is shown to be modular and independently probeable in the same way a human's extra-checklist reasoning is.
